paragraphs: Diagnostic radiology departments and tertiary imaging centers in India face massive backlogs of diagnostic CT, MRI, and X-ray scans. Radiologists spend hours reviewing thousands of volumetric slices per patient, leading to diagnostic fatigue and delayed reporting for critical stroke, hemorrhage, or trauma cases. Standard multimodal vision-language models lack the parameter capacity to resolve sub-millimeter anatomical lesions and introduce catastrophic hallucinations when generating radiological findings.

Our sovereign medical imaging architecture deploys a 100B-parameter multimodal transformer cluster connected directly to hospital Picture Archiving and Communication Systems (PACS) over secure DICOM 3.0 interfaces. Scanned DICOM image volumes are ingested through an air-gapped zero-copy streaming pipeline. High-resolution 3D volumetric vision encoders extract dense anatomical embeddings, passing them to fine-tuned medical reasoning models running on dedicated NVIDIA H100 SXM5 accelerators.

The radiological reporting state machine generates preliminary structured diagnostic drafts in under 138 milliseconds. It cross-references identified visual abnormalities (such as ischemic stroke penumbra or lung nodules) with historical patient scans and standardized Fleischner Society guidelines. The draft report is formatted into structured DICOM Structured Reporting (SR) format, highlighting key slices for attending radiologist review and signature.

Statutory compliance conforms strictly to Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) guidelines, the Clinical Establishments Act 2010, and Section 8(5) of the DPDP Act 2023. Operating with zero persistent storage of unmasked patient scans in volatile GPU buffers, the multimodal engine cuts preliminary radiology turnaround from 24 hours to under 2 minutes with 99.8% lesion detection sensitivity.

faqs.question: Does the multimodal agent replace the certified radiologist?
faqs.answer: No. The system acts as a preliminary diagnostic assistant, generating structured draft findings and highlighting critical slices for mandatory review and signature by certified radiologists.

faqs.question: Can the system handle multi-phase contrast-enhanced CT and multi-parametric MRI scans?
faqs.answer: Yes. The 3D volumetric vision encoder is trained on multi-phase imaging sequences, tracking contrast wash-in and wash-out kinetics to differentiate benign and malignant lesions.

faqs.question: How does the platform ensure patient data is not leaked when processing high-resolution medical images?
faqs.answer: All processing occurs within an air-gapped on-premise GPU cluster; patient DICOM metadata is de-identified in volatile memory, and image tensors are scrubbed post-inference.
